newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southwest spot power higher, Northwest steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southwest spot power higher, Northwest steady.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Southwest moved higher Tuesday in reaction to increased December natural gas contract prices, while Northwest prices were largely steady, market sources said.
"A lot of utilities buy gas in monthly blocks," said one Arizona utility source.
He explained that index prices for December deliveries were about $1.00 per million British thermal units more than the previous month.
"Instead of running gas turbines, we are looking at spot purchases for morning and evening blocks," the trader noted.
In addition, the start last week of a planned refueling outage of the 1,070 megawatt unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in southern California added to the market tone.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Wednesday was quoted at $27.00-28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $25.75-26.25 for Tuesday. Firm, off-peak PV power was near $16.00-17.00.
Next-day firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted at $28.00-29.00 per MWh, up from $25.00-27.00. Off-peak Four Corners was assessed near $16.00-18.00.
In the Northwest, milder temperatures and the Bonneville Power Administration's decision to leave next-day price offers unchanged helped keep the spot market steady, sources said.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Wednesday was assessed at $29.25-29.75 a MWh, unchanged from Monday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Wednesday was quoted at $16.50-17.50, compared with $17.00-18.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was quoted $27.50-29.50, compared with Monday's $28.75-29.25.
Wednesday firm, off-peak power at Mid-C was little changed at $14.00-17.00.
